records.body: Today marks Haiti’s independence from France on this date in 1804, when it became the first country led by former slaves. Haiti’s flag has two bands in the national colors of blue and red, representing the multi-ethnic Haitian people. The white rectangle bears the coat of arms, which shows a palm tree flanked by flags and two cannons, with the motto L'union fait la force (Union Makes Strength). Haiti is the most mountainous nation in the Caribbean, and its name means "Land of Mountains" in the Arawak language.
records.title: Haiti

records.body: Neuschwanstein Castle in Germany is the best-known of the three royal palaces built by King Ludwig II of Bavaria. Often referred to as the paradox castle, it is a medieval-style castle built during the 19th century, when castles were no longer needed for protection and were outfitted with the latest technological comforts, such as an elevator, running water, electricity, telephones, and central heating. The foundation was laid in 1869, and it was inhabitable by 1873, though it was never finished. King Ludwig lived in the castle off and on for six months before his death in 1886. A few weeks after his passing, Neuschwanstein Castle opened to the public as a museum and today welcomes millions of visitors each year.
records.title: Neuschwanstein Castle

records.body: The bronze statue called “The Bear and the Strawberry Tree,” located in the Puerta del Sol square in Spain’s capital city of Madrid, was dedicated on 19 January 1967 and depicts the heraldic symbol of the city. King Alfonso VIII first used this symbol in 1222 as a seal on a decree ending a dispute over land rights between the Catholic Church and the city council. The tree represented the woodlands that the city owned, and the bear represented the animals belonging to the church. Madrid was known in Roman times as Ursalia, or “Land of the Bears,” because of the local bear population.
records.title: The Bear and the Strawberry Tree

records.body: The Basilica di Santa Croce (Basilica of the Holy Cross) in Florence, Italy, is the largest Franciscan church in the world. Construction began in 1294, and it was consecrated in 1442. Many of the basilica’s 16 chapels are decorated with frescos by Giotto and his students, and famous Italians such as Galileo, Machiavelli, and Michelangelo are buried there. In 1982, the Basilica di Santa Croce became a UNESCO World Heritage site as part of the Historic Center of Florence.
records.title: The Basilica di Santa Croce

records.body: The Great Wall of China stretches across the country’s historical northern borders and was built to provide protection against nomadic peoples. Measuring 21,196 km (13,171 mi), the wall begins in the east in Shanhaiguan in Hebei province and ends in Jiayuguan in Gansu province to the west. Beginning in 220 B.C., sections of earlier fortifications were joined together, with additions made over a period of more than 2,000 years. The Great Wall is the world's largest military structure.
records.title: The Great Wall of China

records.body: Located in New York City, New York, the Metropolitan Opera is the largest opera house in the world by capacity, with 3,800 seats and 175 standing room places. Known as “The Met,” it was founded in 1883 and is the largest classical music organization in North America. It moved to its current location at Lincoln Center (pictured) in 1966.
records.title: The Metropolitan Opera House

records.body: Lebanon has had many coats of arms since declaring independence in 1943, but none were officially adopted. The current version is a variation of the national flag. Red stands for the blood shed for liberation, and white for peace, purity, and mountain snow. The cedar tree is the national symbol, embodying eternity, steadiness, happiness, and prosperity.
records.title: Lebanon Coat of Arms

records.body: Established in 1979, the Cayman Islands National Museum occupies the islands’ oldest building, which dates from the 1830s. The museum is dedicated to preserving, researching, and displaying Caymanian heritage and holds over 8,000 artifacts, ranging from coins to a 14-foot catboat.
records.title: The Cayman Islands National Museum

records.body: Poland’s coat of arms was designed in 1927 by noted Polish graphic artist and educator Zygmunt Kaminski. The white crowned eagle is the national symbol, and white and red are the national colors, with white representing purity and truth and red symbolizing courage and the blood shed for freedom.
records.title: Poland’s Coat of Arms

records.body: The American flamingo is one of the largest species of flamingo; an average adult stands 1.5 m (5 ft) tall and weighs 1.8-3.6 kg (4-8 lbs). The birds live in flocks numbering in the thousands in the Caribbean and along the northern coast of South America. The flamingos pictured reside at the Bermuda Aquarium, Museum, & Zoo (BAMZ), owned and operated by the Bermuda government. The BAMZ is one of the world's oldest aquariums and an important center for science education, research, and species conservation.
records.title: The Flamingo

records.body: Hallsgrimskirkja, a Lutheran church in Reykjavik, Iceland, was built between 1945 and 1986 and is one of the country’s tallest buildings, as well as its largest church. Iceland’s volcanoes inspired its unusual design, which resembles a gigantic stalagmite of petrified lava. Reykjavik is the northernmost national capital in the world.
records.title: Hallsgrimskirkja

records.body: Located near Vermillion, South Dakota, Spirit Mound is described in Sioux, Omaha, and Otoe tribal stories as a place where spirits lived. Captain Meriwether Lewis and Second Lieutenant William Clark of the famed Lewis and Clark Expedition climbed the mound on August 25, 1804, and recorded in their report the rocks and wildlife they found and the view of the prairie below. Today Spirit Mound is part of the Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail, which extends from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to Astoria, Oregon
records.title: Spirit Mound

records.body: Adopted in 1988, Malta’s coat of arms has a shield displaying the national flag, with olive and palm branches on each side symbolizing peace. On top of the shield is a golden crown in the shape of a fortification with five turrets, representing Malta's forts. The white ribbon below the shield displays the name Repubblika ta' Malta (Republic of Malta).
records.title: Malta’s Coat of Arms

records.body: The Moravian Church Settlements, one of 28 transnational UNESCO Heritage sites, include settlements in Denmark, Germany, the United Kingdom, and Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. Established in 1741, the Bethlehem location was the most important and first permanent Moravian Church settlement in North America. The settlement’s waterworks (pictured) became America’s first pumped municipal water system when it was built in 1762, and it remained in use until the 1830s. The building is recognized as a National Historic Landmark, Historic Civil Engineering Landmark, and an American Water Landmark.
records.title: The Waterworks
